title: Interleaved requantization shim to minimize dequant tail latency for mixed-precision kernels
creator: Sujay Patel
description:
Background: Production traces show a recurring tail-latency pattern when requests traverse mixed-precision execution paths. When a decode stream switches between INT8-accelerated kernels and FP8 fallback kernels we often pay a nontrivial dequant + requant overhead that is not accounted for by kernel execution time alone. This shows up for short-lived decodes and for workloads that interleave cached KV hits with new prefill segments.

Goal: Implement an interleaved requantization shim in the runtime that reduces dequant tail latency and amortizes casting cost across microbatches without changing numerical outputs beyond current tolerances. The shim should: 1) detect opportunity windows where ephemeral casts can be coalesced across adjacent microbatches and attention heads, 2) schedule tiny inline requant operations near kernel boundaries to avoid full dequantization to FP32, and 3) expose a per-model policy to enable aggressive coalescing for latency-sensitive workloads or conservative single-request accuracy for high-precision SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: P95 end-to-end decode latency for mixed-precision small-batch traces reduced by >= 15% on average compared to baseline on CI benchmarks
No regressions in token-level output fidelity above existing tolerances for validated prompt suite (coverage across proprietary and open prompts)
Feature gated and configurable via model config (requant_window_ms, max_coalesced_batches, head_grouping)
Has unit tests for scheduling correctness and integration tests running on CPU/GPU CI images
Runtime telemetry provides per-request cast-time breakdown and hit/miss counts for coalesced windows
implementation_notes:
High-level approach: 1) Add a lightweight scheduler extension that marks kernel boundary candidates when a mixed-precision switch is imminent (e.g., INT8 -> FP8 or vice versa). 2) Implement an "interleaved requant shim" that performs localized requantization in the kernel-friendly representation (INT8 <-> FP8 internal micro-quantization) without materializing FP32 tensors. 3) Support two modes: coalescing mode (amortize casts across up to N microbatches) and passthrough mode (no coalescing). 4) Integrate with KV cache lifecycle: ensure ephemeral casts do not leak across pinned cache entries and invalidate/rebuild when necessary. 5) Provide a fallback path that forces full dequantization for models flagged as high-precision.

Performance considerations: prefer in-place ephemeral buffers allocated in the kernel workspace, align with existing kernel memory pools, and avoid synchronizations on the critical path. The shim should be microbenchmark-driven and accompanied by assembly-level profiler traces for kernels on NV and AMD backends.
tests: Unit: scheduler state transitions for boundary detection
Unit: correctness of inline requant math against full FP32 dequant/requant reference for representative tensors
Integration: end-to-end synthetic decode comparing latency and outputs for microbatch sizes 1..8
Benchmark: CI perf job across T4/A100/H100 and AMD equivalents with int8-enabled builds
Fuzz: random head-sparsity patterns and KV cache hit/miss cycles
rollout_plan: Feature-gate default off. 1) Merge shim behind flag runtime.requant_shim.enabled=false. 2) Canary on internal dev org traffic with flag enabled for low-volume routes. 3) Collect telemetry for two weeks focusing on P50/P95/P99 and output drift. 4) Gradually enable for latency-critical public tenants with opt-in model config. 5) If any >0.5% of requests report fidelity drift above threshold, rollback for that tenant and capture trace for root cause analysis.
telemetry_requirements: Emit per-request fields: cast_time_ms, coalesced_batches, head_groups_merged, shim_mode (coalesce|passthrough|forced_full). Add aggregated dashboards: cast_time distribution, coalescing hit ratio, and delta of P95 before/after shim. Tag telemetry with model, region, and deployment type (hosted|dedicated|private).
